svg.title: The five classic NFC programming errors — four recoverable, one forever
svg.desc: An error report listing the five most common NFC programming mistakes. Wrong NDEF format: desktop readers parse it, phones ignore it — use NDEF library functions, never raw memory writes. URL too long: an NTAG213 fits roughly 132 URL characters, so test the real production URL. Missing 0xFE terminator TLV: without the terminator byte some phones read garbage — it is one byte, append it. Skipped verification read: read back after every write, because rare times ten thousand tags is not rare. And the only fatal one, highlighted in red: accidental lock — permanent lock bits set by mistake cannot be undone and the tag can only be replaced.
svg.text: FIELD DEBUGGING · THE GREATEST HITS OF "WHY ISN'T THIS WORKING"
Five classic write errors — four recoverable, one forever
ERR
Wrong NDEF format
fix: use NDEF library functions, never raw memory writes
desktop reads it · phones ignore it
ERR
URL too long for the chip
fix: NTAG213 fits ~132 URL characters — test the real production URL
UTM parameters are not free
WARN
Missing 0xFE terminator TLV
fix: append the terminator byte — some phones read garbage without it
it is one byte. append the byte.
WARN
Skipped verification read
fix: read the tag back after every write and compare
"rare" × 10,000 tags = not rare
FATAL
Accidental lock
fix: none — double-check the lock configuration before you hit write
permanent · replace the tag
Four of these cost you an afternoon. The fifth is a small permanent monument to one.
Everything looks fine on the bench — verify before the tags leave the building.
